findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload · Private data: read_ifc_overview, read_ifc_networks, name_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload, ifc_upload_result · Public sink: read_ifc_networks, name_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload, ifc_upload_result · Destructive: water_content_from_vessel, read_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload · Private data: read_ifc_overview, read_ifc_networks, name_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload, ifc_upload_result · Public sink: read_ifc_networks, name_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload, ifc_upload_result · Destructive: water_content_from_vessel, read_ifc_networks, open_ifc_upload

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "size_expansion_vessel" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
